1.author: St. John Chrysostom
1.work: Homilies on the Gospel of St. Matthew, Homily 2
1.text: Why does he call the whole book 'the book of the generation of Jesus Christ,' though it is not this only which the book contains, but all the dispensation? Because this is the sum of the whole dispensation, and is made the root and source of all our blessings. As Moses calls the book of Genesis after the creation of the heaven and earth, although it speaks of many other things, so this evangelist hath named his book from that which is the main point of all the things contained in it.

1.author: St. Jerome
1.text: Notice that he says 'son of David, son of Abraham,' placing David first, though Abraham was the earlier. He does so because the promise made to David, that of his seed Christ should be born, is more recent and more clearly known; whereas the promise to Abraham, being older, was preserved by faith. Both are named, that the reader may know that Christ fulfilled all the promises of God.

23.author: St. John Chrysostom
23.work: Homilies on the Gospel of St. Matthew, Homily 5
23.text: 'They shall call His name Emmanuel.' Whence then is this name? for no one was ever called by such a name. From Scripture custom. For Scripture is wont to give names to things which are coming to pass, as to persons. So when it says, 'They shall call His name Emmanuel,' it means nothing else than that they shall see God among men. For He hath indeed always been among men, but never so manifestly.
